messages:
alex: FYI noticed a regressing p99 on the 8xA100 inference job after the KV prefetch change. +14% p99, throughput down ~23% when sequence len > 1024.

maria: ugh. which model + config?

alex: 30B transformer, TP=2 PP=4, kv-shard=per-stage (we moved to aggressive prefetching across stages). baseline used on-demand per-GPU slice.

david: do you have profiler traces? NCCL/allreduce spikes?

alex: attaching summary from perf-bot below. TL;DR: all-reduce latency increased, overlap with compute reduced. token throughput drop lines up with big all-reduce windows triggered by prefetch bursts.

perf-bot: profile-summary: tokens/s baseline=18.2k, after-prefetch=14.1k; p50 latency baseline=42ms -> 46ms, p99 baseline=230ms -> 263ms; all-reduce mean latency +27% for key-value syncs.

jin: sounds like prefetch caused bigger, more synchronized KV cache fetches across ranks so NCCL batches larger collectives. that kills overlap.

maria: can we change batching heuristic to spread prefetches (jitter) and make smaller async windows?

laura: also check kernel selection for the all-reduce path. we have a fused allreduce kernel that helps small-message scenarios vs default ring. maybe we regressed to ring with recent NCCL bump.

david: good call. alex, can you run this quick probe?

alex: ran two experiments: (1) staggered prefetch with random offset 0-20ms -> throughput improved to 16.9k, p99 down to 245ms. (2) force fused-allreduce path via env var REDWOOD_ALLREDUCE=optimized -> 17.6k tokens/s, p99 238ms. both still worse than baseline but much closer.

maria: interesting — so combination of smaller windows + fused kernel almost recovers. suggests two orthogonal issues: sync pattern and kernel choice.

jin: what about sharding strategy? per-stage slices may increase cross-stage comm. PP stages holding different kv shards will need cross-stage fetches. switching to DP-replicated KV for hot keys might reduce cross-stage all-reduces at cost of memory.

laura: can we try hybrid: replicate top-5% hottest keys across all GPUs (DP) and shard the rest per-stage? reduces hot-key fanout while keeping cold-key memory efficient.

alex: prototype run with hot-replication (top 3%): tokens/s 18.0k, p99 233ms — almost back to baseline. memory uplift ~7% per-GPU.

david: that's promising. we should add metric for "hot-key fanout" in console and alert when prefetch bursts align across ranks.

maria: action items: 1) add jittered prefetch heuristic + default small async window (jin) 2) enable fused allreduce by default for our infra (laura) 3) implement hot-key replication experiment across workloads and measure memory/quality tradeoffs (alex/david) 4) add dashboard + alert for prefetch synchronization (maria).

alex: i'll push perf numbers and a short runbook to the PR. snippet I used for probing:```bash
# run with fused allreduce and staggered prefetch
export REDWOOD_ALLREDUCE=optimized
export KV_PREFETCH_JITTER_MS=20
./run_infer.sh --model redwood-30b --tp 2 --pp 4 --seq 1024 --profile
```

maria: perfect. small follow-up: add a quick e2e that fails if hot-key replication memory > 12% by default so we don't surprise infra.

jin: also add a microbench for all-reduce kernel selection in CI matrix (small msgs, medium msgs, large msgs) so the kernel choice stays tuned after NCCL upgrades.

alex: thanks everyone, will update thread with PR links once I have them. :thumbsup:
